forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Darlington's debt fell by £5.1m but reserves are funding growth in capital spending
news_drafts.lead: Darlington Council reduced its external debt by £5.1m to £167.6m in 2025/26, repaying a maturing loan and taking no new borrowing. The reduction was enabled by slippage of £17.6m in the capital programme, with most delay in housing and regeneration schemes. However, the council's underlying need to borrow for long-lived assets remains substantial at £249.9m. The gap of £73.8m between this capital financing requirement and actual debt is being covered by drawing on cash reserves rather than external borrowing. While this strategy currently saves money because borrowing costs exceed investment returns, the council's investment portfolio shrank to £25m after a forced distribution from its Hermes property fund following a merger. Bank rate cuts stalled at 3.75%, with markets expecting rates to remain static through 2026/27, limiting scope for refinancing savings. The council's treasury budget overspent by £0.8m, driven by lower property fund dividends and changes to repayment schedules for the Feethams House project.

findings.paper_title: Darlington BC - Audit Strategy Memorandum 2025-26 FINAL 021026.pptx
findings.headline: CIPFA Code amendment effective 2025/26 shifts from annual fair value assessment to 5-yearly property revaluations with annual indexation.
findings.detail: HM Treasury has amended the Code effective 1 April 2025. Non-investment property must now be revalued every 5 years with annual indexation in intervening years, rather than being assessed annually for fair value changes. The council will apply judgment in selecting appropriate indices; CIPFA has not prescribed which indices to use.
findings.matters: This material change to property valuation methodology affects 2025/26 accounts and beyond, requiring significant judgment in index selection and potentially affecting year-on-year comparability. Auditors must assess appropriateness of indices applied.
findings.figures: Revaluation cycle: every 5 years; indexation: applied in intervening years (maximum 4 years between revaluations)
findings.quote: The Code has been amended in 2025/26 and now requires other land and buildings to be valued once every 5 years with annual indexation applied to assets during the four intervening years.

findings.paper_title: Darlington BC - Audit Strategy Memorandum 2025-26 FINAL 021026.pptx
findings.headline: Council dwellings valued at £194.509m (down £3.2m from prior year); investment properties at £12.626m (down £0.794m).
findings.detail: Property assets held on the balance sheet have declined in value, with council dwellings falling 1.6% and investment properties falling 5.9%. These revaluations reflect fair value assessments at year-end under CIPFA Code requirements.
findings.matters: Declining asset base affects borrowing capacity and collateral position, particularly where external borrowing is secured against property; also impacts overall balance sheet strength.

findings.paper_title: Darlington BC - Audit Strategy Memorandum 2025-26 FINAL 021026.pptx
findings.headline: Council's net pension position moved to nil in 2025/26 due to IAS 19 asset ceiling restriction of £46.08m.
findings.detail: The Durham County Council Pension Fund reports pension assets of £438.74m against liabilities of £392.66m. However, IAS 19 requires that recognised pension assets cannot exceed the present value of future economic benefits available to the employer. The asset ceiling restriction of £46.08m reduces the net valuation to nil in 2025/26, a material swing from prior year.
findings.matters: This represents a significant change in balance sheet position year-on-year and illustrates the impact of IAS 19 asset ceiling rules on pension-in-surplus funds, affecting how the council's pension position is reported and potentially relevant to borrowing metrics.
findings.figures: 2025/26 pension asset £438.74m; liability £392.66m; asset ceiling restriction £46.08m (2024/25: £36.60m)
findings.quote: In 2025/26, the Council reported a nil net pension valuation due to the application of the assets ceiling 'restriction of surplus' of £46.06m.

findings.paper_title: Darlington BC - Audit Strategy Memorandum 2025-26 FINAL 021026.pptx
findings.headline: General reserves have decreased significantly with rising cost pressures in children's services driven by increased demand and complexity of need.
findings.detail: The Council faces challenging budget pressures and is using reserves to bridge funding gaps. Children's services is identified as the primary driver, with costs rising due to increased demand and case complexity rather than routine inflation. This is flagged by auditors as a significant financial sustainability risk.
findings.matters: Reserve depletion limits financial flexibility; children's services overspends are common across English councils but this council emphasizes demand-driven and complexity-driven cost increases, suggesting above-average structural pressures.
findings.figures: Specific reserve balances and children's services variances not quantified in this audit strategy memorandum
findings.quote: The Council's general reserves have decreased significantly as the Council faces challenging budget pressures. In particular the Council is experiencing rising cost pressure in children's services owing to increased demand and complexity of need.

findings.paper_title: Darlington BC - Audit Strategy Memorandum 2025-26 FINAL 021026.pptx
findings.headline: Auditors will not issue an unmodified opinion until 2028/29; opinions will remain disclaimed or qualified through 2027/28.
findings.detail: Under the 'rebuilding assurance' program, 2026/27 and 2027/28 opinions will be qualified due to lack of assurance over opening balances from prior disclaimed audits. The auditors plan to progressively rebuild assurance across multiple audit cycles, with an unmodified opinion not anticipated before 2028/29.
findings.matters: Four consecutive years without an unmodified opinion (2024/25 through 2027/28) indicates material governance and process challenges that will affect the council's credibility with lenders and stakeholders throughout this period.
findings.figures: 2025/26 disclaimed (30 Jan 2027); 2026/27 qualified (30 Nov 2027); 2027/28 qualified (30 Nov 2028); 2028/29 unmodified (30 Nov 2029)
findings.quote: We will now have assurance over the primary statements and the comparative amounts and will be able to issue an unmodified opinion.
